t: Laozi, meaning 'Old Master', is an honorific and not a personal name; the traditional accounts name him Li Er and describe him as a keeper of the archives at the Zhou court.
By the mid-twentieth century most Western scholars regarded his historicity as doubtful and the Tao Te Ching as a compilation by many hands.
The book teaches the Tao and wu wei, and Laozi became a god in later Taoism and an imperial ancestor under the Tang.
dyk: Taoist myths say that Laozi was conceived when his mother gazed upon a falling star, remained in her womb for 62 years and was born as a grown man with a full grey beard while she leaned against a plum tree.
ev: Traditional accounts place the birth of Laozi, as Li Er, in the state of Chu
The oldest manuscript containing text from the Dào Dé Jīng, on bamboo slips, is written
The oldest complete manuscripts of the Dào Dé Jīng are placed in a tomb at Mawangdui
Sima Qian writes the earliest biographical reference to Laozi in his Records of the Grand Historian
Emperor Gaozong gives Laozi the first of a series of grand temple names
Emperor Xuanzong declares Laozi the Sage Ancestor of the Tang dynasty
Laozi is honoured with the longest of his Tang titles

f.born: In the village of Quren in the state of Chu, present-day Luyi in Henan, as the traditional accounts have it, in the 6th century BCE; the son of the Censor-in-Chief of the Zhou dynasty and Lady Yishou
f.died: Not recorded; in the best-known account he departed west through a frontier gate at the age of 80, and some religious traditions hold that he became an immortal hermit
f.role: Keeper of the Archives for the royal Zhou court in the tradition; regarded by Taoists as the founder of the faith and, in some sects, as a god; historians treat him as a figure of doubtful historicity
f.known: the Tao Te Ching (Dào Dé Jīng); the idea of wu wei; the encounter with Confucius; the departure to the west; the ancestor of the Tang dynasty's rulers; the founding figure of Taoism
